answer: Proof-of-Stake protocols mitigate Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock capital, creating a nebula of economic friction that makes identity forgery expensive. Like shifting sands in a dune, an attacker must acquire significant control of the total supply to gain influence. Each fraudulent identity imposes a cost proportional to the staked value, ensuring that any attempt to flood the system creates a ripple of financial loss that renders large-scale identity replication irrational and unsustainable.
